errors.text: The proposed W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V composition does not match the target Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr family; W and Mo are Group VI rather than Group IV-V transition metals.
LPBF followed by solution annealing and aging replaces the target extrusion of a hydride-bearing ink, hydrogen de-binding, high-vacuum sintering with a titanium oxygen getter, and water quenching.
The hypothesized BCC/B2 nanoprecipitate state is fundamentally different from the target metastable single beta-BCC state retained by quenching to suppress alpha-HCP formation.
The response does not reconstruct sequential hydride decomposition, in-situ alloying, controlled oxygen uptake near 1 wt.%, or the oxygen-scavenging mechanism.

Formation of coherent B2 precipitates in equiatomic LPBF W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V after aging is not established by the cited evidence; the response combines results from distinct alloy systems as a speculative extrapolation.
The target oxidation-resistance route involving a self-healing silicide coating is omitted.
